## Checklist

- [ ] I've considered label spelling variations — "Sodium Laurel Sulfate" and "Sodium Lauryl Sulfate" are genuinely different spellings that both appear on real product labels, so both may need separate entries
- [ ] I've checked for redundant entries; if this ingredient is already in another category, I've explained why the additional classification is intentional

---

> **Note for reviewers:** Matching is case-insensitive — "Sodium Lauryl Sulfate" and "sodium lauryl sulfate" are treated as identical by the tool. Case-only duplicates within one rule can and should be removed. The same ingredient may intentionally appear in different rules when it has multiple relevant classifications; the analyzer shows every matching category and uses the most severe match for the headline verdict.
